items.summary: 23.10.2026 Tiedotteet Ulkoministeri Valtonen tapaa Mongolian ulkoministeri Battsetsegin Helsingissä Ulkoministeri Elina Valtonen ja Mongolian ulkoministeri Batmunkh Battsetseg tapaavat 23. lokakuuta Helsingissä. Ministerit käyvät keskustelun Suomen ja Mongolian kahdenvälisistä suhteista sekä ajankohtaisista ulko- ja turvallisuuspoliittisista asioista. ”On suuri ilo toivottaa ulkoministeri Battsetseg jälleen tervetulleeksi Suomeen. Tapaaminen antaa erinomaisen mahdollisuuden jatkaa keskusteluja, joita kävimme hänen edellisellä vierailullaan reilu vuosi sitten. Työvierailua isännöi tasavallan presidentti Alexander Stubb. Lisätietoja Emma Virkkunen, ulkoministerin erityisavustaja, puh. 0295 350 613 Eevamaria Mielonen, erityisasiantuntija, Itä-Aasian ja Oseanian yksikkö, puh. 0295 350 057 Ulkoministeriön sähköpostiosoitteet ovat muotoa etunimi.sukunimi(a)gov.fi

items.title: Millions of Exploit Attempts Logged Against PHP Servers
items.summary: Attacks targeting the critical PHP vulnerabilities patched Wednesday are mounting as a flood of proof-of-concept exploits appear online. Following a series of leaks, the PHP Foundation on Wednesday released patches for the two flaws, dubbed PHP2Shell, for all currently supported versions of its server-side code (see: Critical PHP Patches Address 'Very, Very Bad Vulnerability'). But the fixes have not suddenly been installed across the internet. "Among the affected hosts whose PHP versions we could identify through Shodan, roughly 99% were still not showing a patched PHP version after 24 hours," said Ox Security on Thursday. Cloud security firm Cloudflare said exploit attempts are flying fast and furious. "In the 10 hours before it was publicly announced, across the Cloudflare network we saw thousands of attempts to exploit it. That jumped to tens of thousands in the 45 minutes post-announcement, hundreds of thousands within two hours, and millions now," said CEO Matthew Prince in a social media post late Wednesday.

items.title: Node.js Brotli Decoder Bug Could Allow Remote Code Execution in All Supported Versions
items.summary: Node.js released security updates on October 21 for its three supported release lines, 22.x, 24.x and 26.x, fixing 10 flaws. The most serious is a bug in the Brotli decompression code that Node.js bundles, which the project says can allow remote code execution, meaning an attacker could run code of their choosing on the affected system. Each supported line has one fixed version: 22.23.4 and 24.22.1 on the long-term support lines, and 26.12.1 on the current line. Node.js 20.x and earlier have reached end of life and will not receive the fix, so they should be moved to a supported line. The Brotli flaw is in code Node.js bundles, not in a user's own program. Node.js runs that code whenever it decompresses Brotli data, either directly through the node:zlib module or automatically when code calls fetch() on a response sent with Brotli compression. An application is exposed where it decompresses Brotli data an attacker controls, such as a request body or a response fetched from another server.

items.title: Exploring the Risks and Impacts of AI on Vulnerability Discovery and Exploitation
items.summary: As we hear a lot of noise about AI’s impact on vulnerability discovery and exploitation, I found the need to compartmentalize the risks. So, I took it upon myself to build categories that provide a mental framework for the risks, impact, and evidence AI poses for vulnerabilities and exploitation. Most of these risks aren't new. AI makes the capabilities behind each one more accessible and accelerates how quickly attackers can use them. A growing risk category is AI-assisted vulnerability discovery: AI tools, including frontier models and purpose-built harnesses for finding vulnerabilities, have become accessible to the masses, requiring less skill and making it much easier to discover software vulnerabilities. This accessibility isn't limited to defenders. Attackers have the same capabilities at their disposal, allowing them to discover and exploit new zero-days and expand the pool of viable targets.

items.title: PHP blames supply chain security biz Chainguard for putting huge chunks of the web at risk
items.summary: PHP developers have accused software supply chain security shop Chainguard of effectively revealing critical bugs in the open-source scripting language ahead of a planned official disclosure. On Wednesday, just hours after releasing emergency patches for the two bugs collectively called PHP2shell, PHP maintainers published a blog about how the vulnerabilities were found and fixed. They credited researchers at Calif, OpenAI, and Wiz with finding the security holes between August and September. All three companies have said they used AI models to find the vulnerabilities, which are now tracked as CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, and can allow an unauthenticated attacker to execute code on servers running PHP. This is especially serious because PHP powers huge chunks of the public web. It also adds a dose of irony to the “leak and disrupted disclosure” part of the blog, which blames Chainguard - a company that aims to secure software supply chains by hardening open source code - for the messy disclosure.

items.title: Arista patches new VeloCloud Orchestrator zero-day exploited in attacks
items.summary: Arista Networks released security updates to patch an actively exploited zero-day vulnerability affecting VeloCloud Orchestrator (VCO) On-Prem deployments. VCO is a web-based management portal that helps administrators configure, monitor, and manage VeloCloud SD-WANs (Software-Defined Wide Area Networks) and associated edge devices. Tracked as CVE-2026-114625, this critical-severity flaw can allow attackers with basic privileges, access to the VCO web interface, and a valid authenticated session to escalate privileges through low-complexity SQL injection attacks that don't require user interaction. "VeloCloud Orchestrator (VCO) on-prem has a security issue where this issue may allow a remote attacker to access privileged internal functionality and impact the VCO host. Successful exploitation may compromise the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of the orchestrator and data managed by the orchestrator," Arista said. "On an affected system, any authenticated user can gain operator privileges and masquerade as a local 'superuser operator' user. This includes access to functionality that is intended for internal use only and which is not intended to be remotely accessible."

items.title: WordPress Core <= 7.0.2 - Authenticated (Contributor+) Stored Cross-Site Scripting via Quick Edit
items.summary: Classification: Important, Solution: Official Fix, Exploit Maturity: Not Defined, CVSSv3.1: 4.9, CVEs: CVE-2026-114570, Summary: WordPress Core is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via Quick Edit in all versions up to, and including, 7.0.2 due to insufficient escaping of user display names. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with Contributor-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a higher privileged user accesses the affected administrative screens. This issue only affects sites with a large number of users.

items.title: The Current Landscape of OAuth Attacks
items.summary: As enterprises continue to roll out multi-factor authentication (MFA), attackers have adapted. Rather than only stealing credentials, attackers have shifted to stealing Open Authorization (OAuth) tokens, the keys that govern what applications can do on your behalf. Adversaries are already accelerating these attacks by using dynamic evasion code, phishing-as-a-service (PhaaS) templates and LLM-generated brand impersonations. Because OAuth attacks occur at the authorization layer after user authentication, stolen access and refresh tokens bypass MFA, survive password resets and grant durable access. To understand why OAuth has become such a prime target for modern adversaries, it helps to examine the authentication challenges the protocol was originally designed to solve. Looking back at how applications handled identity before OAuth reveals how the threat landscape has evolved from simple password theft to complex token hijacking.

items.title: How APT41 revived the BlackLotus bootkit to attack diplomatic organizations in Central Asia
items.summary: Back in October 2022, Kaspersky GReAT was looking into a peculiar advertisement on a hacking forum. A cybercriminal had been advertising a UEFI bootkit, dubbed BlackLotus, that could bypass Secure Boot, for $5,000. Given the low price for such powerful capabilities, the cybersecurity community initially took this advertisement with a grain of salt. As no BlackLotus samples were found in the wild, no one could at the time verify the claims made in the forum post. However, about half a year later, in March 2023, ESET confirmed that the BlackLotus advertisement was genuine. The researchers tracked down samples of this bootkit and confirmed that it can indeed bypass Secure Boot through a vulnerability called Baton Drop (CVE-2022-21894). As this vulnerability was still exploitable in 2023, Microsoft had to release multiple security updates to address it. Since the release of these updates, the BlackLotus bootkit has gone quiet — no publicly known attacks have used it. Yet in early 2026, we discovered a malware sample similar to BlackLotus that was used in an APT campaign in Central Asia. In this report, we share our findings, including new payloads and possible attribution of this campaign.

items.title: WatchGuard Agent Incorrect Permission Assignment in Log Directory Allows Local Log Tampering
items.summary: Classification: Severe, Solution: Official Fix, Exploit Maturity: Not Defined, CVSSv3.1: 7.3, CVEs: CVE-2026-115253, Summary: An incorrect permission assignment vulnerability in the WatchGuard Agent's log directory allows a local, authenticated non-administrative user to create, modify, append to, or delete the agent's log files and write other files into the directory. This allows an attacker to tamper with or destroy the agent's security logs and stage further local attacks by placing executable content in a directory owned by a privileged service.

items.title: Max-severity GitLab bug allows remote code execution over 12 years of releases
items.summary: GitLab on Wednesday patched a maximum-severity flaw that could allow unauthenticated attackers to execute arbitrary code on self-managed servers under certain conditions. Affected software releases date back a full 12 years - so upgrade to a fixed version now. The integer overflow bug, tracked as CVE-2026-110264, affects regular-expression compilation in GitLab Community Edition (CE) and Enterprise Edition (EE), including versions dating back to GitLab 7.0, released in June 2014. The flaw, “under certain conditions, could have allowed an unauthenticated user to execute arbitrary code on the GitLab server due to integer overflow when compiling a specially crafted regular expression,” the vendor said in its release notes. GitLab released fixes in versions 19.5.1, 19.4.3, and 19.3.6, and backported the patch to versions 19.2.9, 19.1.9, 19.0.10, and 18.11.13. The vendor “strongly recommends” that all organizations running vulnerable software upgrade to a fixed version “as soon as possible.”

items.title: Two CVSS 9.0 Linux KSMBD RCE Flaws Disclosed on Public Mailing Lists Before Kernel Fixes
items.summary: Linux servers running KSMBD, the kernel's built-in SMB server, are exposed to two publicly reported remote code execution flaws rated 9.0 by Trend Micro's Zero Day Initiative, with no fix yet in the mainline kernel. One of them, ZDI-CAN-33774, can be triggered before any network authentication. The other, ZDI-CAN-33549, requires the SMB Direct transport and an RDMA-capable network interface. ZDI-CAN-33549 is an integer underflow in KSMBD's SMB Direct path. A client can supply RDMA buffer descriptors in which the first is longer than the declared payload, causing the server's size counter to wrap and allowing a subsequent memory copy to overrun the end of an allocated buffer. It requires three things: an RDMA-capable interface (hardware or the rxe software driver), a writable KSMBD share, and a client negotiating SMB Direct. ZDI-CAN-33774 requires no authentication, exposing any server running KSMBD on port 445. The flaw is a race in how KSMBD assigns its handler table: a burst of short SMB1 packets followed by an SMB2 packet in the same TCP write causes workers to handle SMB1 data with an SMB2 handler, reading past the end of the shorter buffer. A path to writing past the buffer also exists once an attacker has access to a share.

items.title: TiDB Breach Exposes Flawed Cloud Security Assumptions
items.summary: A breach of an open source database provider may have inadvertently highlighted a serious gap in the way companies think about their cloud security. On Oct. 19, software maker PingCAP, which sells an SQL database program called TiDB, disclosed that it had been breached. According to PingCAP's website, it serves major American corporations like Atlassian, Square, and Pinterest, as well as major players in China's AI space, including Manus, Kimi, and more. The perpetrator — the somewhat deceptively named "Fulcrum Security," or FulcrumSec, for short — is a relatively new extortionist group whose leak site already includes major organizations like LexisNexis, Novo Nordisk, and the Manchester Airports Group (MAG). Earlier this fall, FulcrumSec appears to have compromised PingCAP, enjoying something shy of unfettered access to all of its cloud management, financial, analytics, storage, and other systems for a month or more.

items.title: Japan's Onamae Desktop Cloud hacked, up to 27,000 servers affected
items.summary: Hackers compromised the infrastructure of Onamae Desktop Cloud, a popular provider of VPS services in Japan, and installed malware on up to 26,739 customers' servers. The company confirmed on October 20 that an unauthorized third party installed "malicious programs" in some customer environments.After detecting the intrusion, the company says it progressively shut down customer servers beginning at 04:00 local time on October 21, 2026. “We have confirmed that unauthorized access by a third party occurred against Onamae.com Desktop Cloud and that unauthorized programs were installed in some customers’ server environments,” reads the announcement. Onamae.com, operated by GMO Internet, a member of GMO Internet Group, is one of Japan’s largest domain registrars and also provides web hosting, DNS, and other internet infrastructure services. Its Desktop Cloud byGMO service is advertised as "ideal for stable FX automated trading, including continuous operation of MetaTrader 4 (MT4)." According to the alert, the breach may have exposed data stored on the impacted servers. However, the company has not confirmed any instance of information being misused or leaked. The company also emphasizes that payment information, such as credit card details, is not affected because it is stored on a different infrastructure. As the investigation continues and more details become available, GMO says it will provide updates.

items.title: Compromised eMudhra intermediate certificates
items.summary: Cisco Talos is aware of eight compromised intermediate certificates belonging to the intermediate certificate authority, eMudhra. Rather than possessing the mandatory 384 bits of pseudo-random security, several private keys evaluated single-digit and double-digit integers. This misconfiguration allows an attacker with the private key of any of the compromised intermediate CAs to impersonate any website or service. Six of the TLS certificates, trusted by Chrome, Mozilla, and Apple have been blocked by these vendors already. Two other certificates, used for codesigning by Microsoft, have also been blocked. Talos expects there will be additional patches available across a variety of technologies as software applications work to remediate the certificates’ exposure. Following the disclosure, eMudhra has revoked the compromised certificates and stopped issuing new certificates under its G3 root. The cause of this issue, originated during an April 30, 2025 key generation activity conducted by eMudhra under its emSign Root TLS CA - G3 and cross-signed Comodo AAA Certificate Services. During a key generation ceremony for 24 subordinate CAs, a flaw in eMudhra’s key generation process created a second set of weak P-384 keys during a wrap/unwrap step. Those keys were mistakenly used for eight intermediate CA certificates. This flaw took the encryption from 384 bytes of entropy down to 3 – 8, making recovering the private keys trivial.
